title: GitHub Copilot: The World's Most Widely Adopted AI Developer Tool
talk_summary: A GitHub DevRel advocate demos Copilot's evolution from IDE autocomplete to chat, extensions, and Enterprise features (repo indexing, knowledge bases, PR summaries).

takeaways.what_they_do: Enterprise lets you select repos to index so chat can locate functions and their callers across the whole solution rather than guessing from open files.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this repository has been indexed for improved understanding and accuracy so with GitHub co-pilot Enterprise you go through and pick what repos you want to index

takeaways.technique: Markdown knowledge bases as scoped retrieval
takeaways.what_they_do: Knowledge bases are collections of markdown files in repos that chat can be explicitly pointed at to get project-specific answers instead of generic ones.
takeaways.evidence_quote: knowledge bases are collections of markdown files that are stored right inside of your repos themselves

takeaways.what_they_do: Reviewer uses the linked user story as intent and asks Copilot to explain the diff, then judges whether the implementation matches the stated intent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: by looking at the user story I know what the intent was now does co-pilot agree that the what's actually implemented matches that intent

takeaways.technique: Auto-generated PR summary and per-file change list
takeaways.what_they_do: Copilot generates a summary paragraph plus file-by-file change descriptions into the PR body from the diff.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's going to look at all the changes that you've made provide a nice summary paragraph and then file by file list out all of the changes

takeaways.what_they_do: When generating API-integration code, Copilot flags that API keys must not be hardcoded and points to vault/secrets stores.
takeaways.evidence_quote: make sure you do not hardcode that API key in your code make sure you store that in hashy corp Vault or Azure key Vault or GitHub Secrets
